answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before joining a market, then slash that stake when an independently verifiable task is shown to be fraudulent. A sybil operator must fund every fake identity separately; multiplying accounts no longer creates free influence. The stake can be released after a challenge window, so honest agents retain access while attackers risk losing capital and paying the opportunity cost of keeping it locked. A vine of copied profiles still has to pass through this quartz-gated inlet.
